result_1.name: Temporal Snapshot Indistinguishability / External Freshness Requirement
result_1.statement: If a verifier's entire trusted state is rollbackable with the experiment snapshot, a previously valid snapshot cannot be distinguished locally from genuinely being at that earlier valid state. Hash chains and signatures authenticate the presented state/history but cannot prove that a later valid suffix existed and was erased.
result_1.key_counterexample: Every stale valid prefix of a six-event hash chain passed local verification after rollback, while a freshness root outside the rollback domain rejected each stale prefix.
result_1.novelty_boundary: Known secure-logging/rollback-protection principle; not claimed as new computer-science mathematics. JANUS contribution under review is integration as a mandatory causal-evidence gate for independent-future experiments.

result_2.name: Authenticity / Freshness Separation
result_2.statement: A cryptographically valid old checkpoint remains authentic after rollback; validity of its signature does not establish that it is the latest state.
result_2.implication: Scientific evidence must carry an independently rooted freshness relation, not only content integrity and signatures.

result_3.name: Fork / Split-History Requirement
result_3.statement: Two branches sharing the same valid prefix can each be locally valid. Detecting equivocation requires an external single-head rule, consistency proof, gossip, quorum comparison or equivalent mechanism outside the forked local view.

result_4.name: Crash-Recovery Evidence State Machine
result_4.rule: A crash must never silently promote an unanchored or locally incomplete trial into anomaly evidence.

result_5.name: Rollback-Domain Rule
result_5.statement: A counter, nonce registry, checkpoint cache or key that is restored by the same snapshot cannot serve as the sole anti-rollback root for that snapshot.
acceptable_roots_examples: transparency log with independently compared heads/gossip

prior_art_boundary.secure_logging: Rollback/crash resistance is established computer-security prior art; adaptive crash attacks and protected-state requirements have been studied.
prior_art_boundary.monotonic_counters: Trusted monotonic state is an established anti-replay/anti-rollback technique, subject to hardware/platform limitations.
prior_art_boundary.transparency_gossip: Independent comparison/gossip of append-only log views is established for detecting split views/equivocation.

next_gate: Design and machine-test a multi-witness external bench continuity protocol with witness faults, stale/offline witnesses, quorum rules, split-view attacks, and exactly defined trust assumptions.
